newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia's Megawati denies alliance with rivals.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia's Megawati denies alliance with rivals.

text.p: The ousted leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) denied on Sunday that a formal alliance existed between her backers and the country's other minority party contesting general elections set for May 29.

Megawati Sukarnoputri, 51, deposed last year as the officially-recognised PDI leader by government-backed dissidents in her party, said instructions she gave to her supporters last month not to take part in the election campaign still stood.
Some of her backers appear to have moved into the ranks of the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP). Banners proclaiming "Mega-Bintang" have appeared at PPP rallies.
Bintang (star) is the symbol of the PPP.

"They create a kind of name, Mega-Bintang, but actually the real coalition (between) PDI and PPP has not...happened," said Megawati, the popular elder daughter of Indonesia's late founding president Sukarno.
"I would just like to explain to you that this is really quite spontaneous," she told Reuters in an interview.

The Christian-nationalist PDI, the PPP and the ruling Golkar are the only parties legally entitled to run for the 425 elected seats in the House of Representatives. The other 75 seats are reserved for the military who do not vote.
The government has rejected Megawati's list of candidates for the vote, only accepting those of her rival, deputy parliamentary speaker Surjadi, as the PDI's recognised leader.
The PDI split appears to have damaged the party's electoral hopes, with PDI rallies throughout the country attracting dismal attendance compared to gatherings of PPP and Golkar supporters.
Golkar, guaranteed a substantial majority, is seeking to raise its percentage of the poll to over 70 percent from the 68 percent it received in the last election in 1992.
The PPP received 17 percent and the PDI 15 percent of the vote last time round.
The PPP has provided the main challenge to Golkar and last week the government moved to ban the use of any banners or posters using the words "Mega-Bintang".
It also banned the use of pictures or images of Megawati.
During campaigning in Jakarta on Sunday, however, PPP supporters continued to use Mega-Bintang paraphernalia and street vendors sold pictures of her at traffic lights.
"I think it is an exaggerated thing that the government has tried to ban as it is really very spontaneous, it is the creativity of the people," Megawati said.
She said she would issue new instructions soon on what she wanted her supporters to do on election day.

"I will give my instruction before May 29 and now they are really waiting for that. I will give this maybe 10 days or a week before the election. It is still secret, so please just wait for that," Megawati said.
However, she indicated she would not call for an illegal boycott of the election.
